newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees Bosnian mine-clearing programme.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees Bosnian mine-clearing programme.

text.p: The European Commission said on Friday it had agreed with government officials in Bosnia and Herzegovina on a plan for helping to clear the country's three million anti-personnel mines.

The European Union executive said it would provide six million European currency units ($7.6 million) to purchase mine-clearing equipment, pay for 240 local mine clearers and create a rapid-response Explosive Ordnance Disposal unit.
Land mines in Bosnia cause 100 casualties every month, and engineers from the NATO-led peacekeeping force IFOR estimate that only half of the country's minefields have been identified.
"Minefields stand in the way of vital infrastructure repairs and limit agricultural production," Donato Chiarini, the EU's special envoy to Bosnia, said in the statement.
The Commission said 70 percent of the money would go to Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation and 30 percent to its Serb Republic.
